title: ALBERT factorized embedding with latent-domain Mirror views
hypothesis: A small domain-specific Givens view applied inside ALBERT's low-dimensional token embedding bottleneck can recover held-out domain-token embedding behavior with fewer complete bytes than a generic dense bottleneck adapter and independent per-domain tables, while outperforming hard factorized sharing and output-side FiLM.
physical_object: One fixed 128x8 low-dimensional token embedding table and one fixed 8x16 factorized embedding projection, shared by eight domains.
mirror_coordinate: Four learned domain-specific Givens angles applied to the eight-dimensional token embedding before the shared projection to dimension 16.
logical_multiplicity: Eight domain functions over 128 token IDs (1,024 logical outputs) generated by one shared factorized embedding plus 32 domain-view scalars.
prior_art_delta: PA61 ALBERT uses low-dimensional factorized embeddings and hard parameter sharing. This experiment tests whether a Mirror coordinate inserted inside the embedding bottleneck restores domain functions more cheaply than hard sharing, output-side FiLM, or a generic dense latent adapter.

methods: independent per-domain full embedding oracle (all pairs; storage upper control)
ALBERT-style shared low-dimensional embedding and projection
factorized embedding plus output-side domain FiLM scale/shift
factorized embedding plus generic dense 8x8 latent transform per domain
factorized embedding plus four domain Givens Mirror angles in the latent bottleneck

teacher.factorization: A fixed seeded 128x8 token table is transformed by a fixed seeded 8x16 projection; both are charged for every factorized method.
teacher.domain_functions: The teacher applies four disjoint 2D rotations in the 8D latent space before projection. Domain 0 is the identity anchor. Other domain angles are seeded random values.
teacher.split: A deterministic seeded 80/20 token-domain split; every token has at least one observed domain and every domain has observed tokens. Train domain transforms only on observed pairs and report train/held-out separately.
teacher.task_quality: A fixed seeded 16x16 decoder maps teacher outputs to 16 classes. Report embedding NRMSE and decoder NLL/top-1 on observed and held-out pairs.
teacher.oracle_boundary: The independent table oracle stores every teacher output and is a storage/quality upper control only; it is not held-out generalization evidence.

development.selection_metric: Held-out embedding NRMSE is primary; held-out decoder NLL/top-1, observed-pair quality, actual total payload bytes, operation proxies and runtime are secondary.
development.allowed_tuning: No tuning planned. Fixed dimensions, teacher, split, training schedule and optimizer. Correctness-only fixes can rerun development before fresh access.

fresh.open_gate: Both development worlds: Mirror held-out NRMSE <=0.03; dense latent control <=0.03; Mirror within 0.005 NRMSE of dense; Mirror payload <=0.80x dense payload and <=0.10x full oracle; Mirror improves held-out NRMSE over output FiLM by >=0.01 and hard sharing by >=0.05; observed NRMSE <=0.03; exact payload replay. Otherwise fresh stays sealed.
fresh.fresh_success: All three fresh worlds satisfy all held-out, simple-control, complete-byte and exact-replay gates.

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: full independent domain-token embedding table or shared 128x8 table and 8x16 projection
domain latent dense matrices, FiLM scales/shifts or Mirror angles
storage.deterministic_reconstruction: Domain/token indices and fixed Givens plane order are determined by dimensions; no pair-address list is stored.

success_gate: All three fresh worlds satisfy held-out quality, hard-sharing/FiLM improvement, dense transform byte ratio, full-table byte ratio and exact replay.
failure_gate: Any development held-out quality, observed-quality, simple-control or total-payload gate fails.
boundaries: synthetic factorized embedding proxy, not a pretrained ALBERT checkpoint, language-model, or natural domain transfer result
shared low-dimensional table and projection are fixed to isolate domain-view insertion
teacher is aligned to latent Givens rotations
fixed update budget is not a capacity/near-convergence claim
